title: Certificate Rotation, Expiry, and Failure Recovery Lab Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies certificate rotation, expiry, and failure recovery lab?
options: Model the installed-version compatibility matrix and establish overlapping trust before changing the served chain.
Rotate server first and release later
Use remote config through the pinned host as sole recovery
Remove old pins based only on latest-version availability
questions.answer: Model the installed-version compatibility matrix and establish overlapping trust before changing the served chain.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Publishing a compatible app update guarantees that all active users can connect after rotation.
questions.explanation: Rotating the server to a new key before an adopted mobile release trusts it immediately locks every older pinned client out.

questions.prompt: What invariant prevents a pinning outage?
questions.answer: Every supported installed client and every served chain must share at least one acceptable pin.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
